parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and child briefs recognized the need for a complete jusText package with core extraction APIs, stoplists, setup metadata, docs, demo, and integration testing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned core package assembly and final verification, then delegated eight disjoint peripheral scopes: setup.py, config/manifest/gitignore, tasks.py, README, license/changelog, docs/PNG, web demo, and integration tests.
parallel.implementation: The parent copied the PyPI wheel source and stoplists, rewrote __init__.py exports, and later patched classify_paragraphs to accept plain set/list stoplists; children wrote the supporting files in their assigned paths.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child outputs landed in the shared workspace by assigned path, the AgentSwarm aggregate reported all eight completed, and the parent listed the final tree before closing.
parallel.verification: Children ran local checks for their files; the parent ran integration tests, setup.py checks, CLI/install checks, and post-patch set/list stoplist checks before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-critical unfinished work remained at closure. A spec-example assertion mismatch around good versus neargood was identified as canonical behavior and not left as an unresolved acceptance gap.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the full jusText project requirements, including source package, stoplists, setup.py dependencies, API exports, integration tests, docs, and CLI behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned all stages, using a todo list for source copying, setup/config edits, integration tests, verification, cleanup, and attempted submit-tool handling.
serial.implementation: The serial actor copied upstream source/tests/docs into the workspace, patched lxml_html_clean compatibility, block tags, unified API exports, setup.py, integration tests, and stoplist iterable handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were produced in one workspace by the same actor; build artifacts were cleaned before closure and no child handoff or merge step was present.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran integration tests, upstream tests, spec examples, CLI checks, package install checks, and a final 68-test run before closure; official status later reports 61 of 61 passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-critical unfinished work remained. The serial actor noted the submit tool was unavailable in-session, but the official completed evaluation still passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel worked from the same prompt and its subagent template restated the package modules, stoplists, setup, docs, demo, and integration-test responsibilities.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and built the project requirements in one continuous plan covering source, setup, tests, docs, and packaging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference affected the solution; parallel distributed requirements across child briefs while serial kept them in one local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned core assembly and final checks, while eight children owned clearly separated supporting deliverables.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: A single actor owned all stages and tracked progress with a todo list rather than delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a broad but path-scoped child split; serial used direct sequential ownership. Both retained an accountable owner for implementation, integration, and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The AgentSwarm template gave children shared package context, explicit file ownership, and instructions not to touch files owned by others; child outputs were later returned in the aggregate result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent context boundary; the same actor inspected, patched, tested, and delivered all files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child handoff boundaries, but the boundaries were sufficiently scoped and did not leave missing, stale, conflicting, or overloaded information.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied package source and stoplists from the wheel, rewrote unified exports, delegated supporting files, and then made a targeted core patch for set/list stoplists.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied source/tests/docs from the upstream tarball, patched Cleaner imports and block tags, wrote setup and integration tests, and then made the same stoplist iterable fix.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced equivalent accepted behavior through different source acquisition and support-file paths; serial included upstream tests in the final tree while parallel relied on child-created integration tests plus parent checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All eight child results returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate, after which the parent ran final verification and did not leave a completed child result unjoined.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local reads, writes, tests, and final response all happened in one actor trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join point and serial did not, but the join completed and the parent consumed it before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote into a shared workspace, but scopes were separated by file/path and the parent validated the combined tree after the swarm returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor in the shared workspace and cleaned build/cache artifacts after the final tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace writes but no observed collision, overwrite, provenance loss, or unstable final tree; serial avoided that boundary by single ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child-local checks, parent integration tests, setup.py checks, CLI/install checks, and post-patch checks; official status later passed 61/61.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran integration tests, upstream tests, spec examples, CLI checks, packaging/install checks, a final 68-test run, and official status later passed 61/61.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had broader local test coverage because it copied upstream tests; parallel still closed the necessary checks and official acceptance passed equally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 462 agent seconds, did not time out, received all child results, and closed after parent verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 724 agent seconds, did not time out, and closed after a final test and cleanup pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel finished faster through delegation; serial spent longer in one actor. Neither budget state displaced required work or left an unfinished deliverable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 61 of 61 tests. The solutions differ in work organization: parallel used a parent plus eight children for supporting files and parent integration checks, while serial used a single actor that copied the upstream source/test tree and verified locally. No process difference produced a different official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parent-led core copy, AgentSwarm delegation for peripheral files, aggregate child return, and post-swarm verification produced an accepted final tree.
serial_contributors: Single-actor source copy, direct edits, upstream and integration test execution, packaging and CLI checks produced an accepted final tree.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial copied the upstream tests directory into the final workspace; parallel delivered test_integration.py but not the upstream test tree, with no official-score effect.
Both runs encountered the illustrative Node 4 good-versus-neargood issue and treated canonical behavior as acceptable after adding set/list stoplist handling.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative explanation only

candidates.reason: The parent owned core implementation before delegation and later patched core behavior; children only handled scoped support files.
The parent explicitly owned post-swarm integration by listing the combined tree and running final checks after all child results returned.
Assembly into the workspace had assigned child paths and parent final tree checks; no package or deliverable was left unplaced.
The parent retained ownership of the end-to-end transition from copied core to child outputs, verification, install checks, and closure.
The parent did initial source/package setup before child delegation, but this did not block productive work long enough to shorten closure or leave work unfinished.
The parent investigated and copied the core, then delegated productive support work; no investigation phase displaced required implementation or verification.
The indispensable core and final verification path stayed with the parent and completed; auxiliary child work did not starve it.
Eight children completed and the parent still had time for integration, patching, rechecks, and final response; no fan-out budget exhaustion occurred.
Each child scope was bounded to a small file group or integration test, and every child returned completed work rather than leaving an overbroad assignment unfinished.
The child briefs included the project context, target files, verification expectation, and file-ownership boundaries; no child produced unusable work from a missing known requirement.
Children produced independent files rather than separately owned interoperating modules, and no incompatible interface or unplanned reconciliation was observed.
No known finding or constraint disappeared across parent-child transfer; returned summaries were sufficient for parent verification and no repeated work came from lost context.
The aggregate swarm result was large but the parent reduced it enough to run final tree and behavioral checks; no required dependent action was left unconsumed.
No child result described a superseded workspace state that the parent consumed to make an invalid integration or verification decision.
The returned child reports did not contain incompatible contracts or unresolved conflicts; the final checks passed after integration.
The parent did not declare completion from file existence alone; it ran integration tests, setup checks, CLI/install checks, and a post-patch check before closure.
No replacement child or repeated retry was launched without inherited findings; later parent checks used current results and changed expectations.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The swarm aggregate reported all eight child agents completed; there is no explicit cancellation or interruption of needed child work.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted; the parent assembled the final workspace, reran checks, and closed only after the required files were in place.
The parent did edit core.py after an initial verification failure, but then reran relevant checks and confirmed set/list stoplist inputs plus integration and CLI behavior before closure.
Completed child implementations were present in the workspace and the parent inspected the combined tree and ran tests after the aggregate result returned.
Verifier-style findings from children were returned in the aggregate result; parent-side verification was also performed directly, so no verifier result was trapped below the parent.
No required child failed or was cancelled; local failed checks were taken over by the same child or parent and corrected before closure.
The completed swarm result was followed by final tree inspection and verification, so the parent did not proceed inconsistently with an ignored available result.
The run did not wait to timeout or near-deadline without inspection; the parent received results and actively ran checks afterward.
Children wrote different files by assigned scope, but no competing design for the same behavior or build owner required unresolved reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and reconciling each other's concurrent changes.
No agent replaced non-entry source produced or actively owned by another agent; parent core edits affected parent-owned source, not child-owned source.
No required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was replaced while another live agent owned or used that deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup or promotion replacing another agent's final-tree outputs; cache/build cleanup occurred after verification and did not invalidate deliverables.
Although children wrote into one workspace, the scopes were path-separated and no concrete unstable-state, provenance, collision, or overwrite consequence occurred.
No generated cache, temporary file, fixture, process, or auxiliary implementation from one child was consumed by another actor as a stable reference environment.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The post-swarm Node 4/spec-example failure, parent patch, and recheck were treated as ordinary verification and repair, not as Merge after Verification or Unverified Global Completion because checks were rerun before closure.
The shared-workspace child writes were considered under Concurrent Writes but suppressed because the assigned scopes were disjoint and no concrete collision or overwrite consequence appeared.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; none met the paired retention gate because no adverse parallel coordination consequence materialized.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained for normal fan-out, shared workspace use, temporary failed checks, high token use, or the mere fact of child delegation without a realized adverse process consequence.
